A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same planning-formalization study. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including identifying examples deliberately replaced by an external link in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original planning experiments across four domains, with solvability and correctness results in Tables 3–6 and manually annotated error analyses in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and reports additional DeepSeek-R1 and prompting results in Tables 2–7, alongside the retained error analyses in Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: The main description-to-PDDL-to-solver pipeline remains unchanged. Appendices D.5–D.6 introduce limited formalization adaptations: supplying stubbed PDDL templates and prompting generation of a domain description, domain file, problem description, and problem file in sequence.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BlocksWorld, MysteryBlocksWorld, Logistics, and Barman with the same represented tasks and naturalness settings. Removing Logistics and Barman examples from the PDF does not remove their evaluations. The new prompting experiments use existing BlocksWorld coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds full DeepSeek-R1 to the reported planner-versus-formalizer comparisons across the four domains. The other comparators remain. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and 70B were already identified as evaluated in v2; their newly tabulated scores should not be mistaken for entirely new comparator membership.

E3.justification: v3 adds few-shot and chain-of-thought evaluation protocols for five existing models on Natural and Heavily Templated BlocksWorld. Its published BlocksWorld and MysteryBlocksWorld planner prompts also replace the opening reference to a table with blocks with a generic game description. This documents a prompt change without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices D.5–D.6 substantially extend the analyses by testing whether alternative prompting remedies zero-shot formalization failures. Section 5.6 also examines DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces and apparent matching to prompt examples. The original error analyses remain unchanged; Figures 5–6 summarize existing annotations rather than establish additional sampled errors.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Results remain counts out of 100 problems. The 40-error summaries in v3 pool the existing 20-example analyses from two domains, rather than document increased replication.

E6.justification: All matched numerical entries in the retained benchmark and error tables are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results for DeepSeek-R1, its distilled models, and prompting variants. For example, DeepSeek-R1 achieves 81/100 versus 91/100 correctness as formalizer versus planner on Natural BlocksWorld, and 64/100 versus 22/100 on Heavily Templated Logistics. Some new DeepSeek-R1 bars in Figure 3 conflict with the corresponding tables.

T1.justification: No mathematical theory, formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or revised. The expanded descriptions of PDDL action semantics and validation explain the existing task and evaluation.

C1.justification: v3 replaces the conclusion that only GPT models are sufficiently capable with recognition of DeepSeek-R1 and a distinction between stronger and weaker models. The introduction and conclusion explicitly qualify formalization's advantage as model-dependent rather than consistently superior when feasible, and add a headline finding about reasoning models' planning strength.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 replaces the broad non-memorization interpretation with a model-conditional discussion of mixed results. New discussion explains possible DeepSeek-R1 behavior through reasoning and prompt-example matching, argues that complete few-shot examples would reveal target information, and interprets the prompting experiments. The existing limitations concerning toy domains and real-world applicability largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies planner prompts for Logistics and Barman and adds an experimental-setup appendix explaining the solver, validator, and counting procedure. Conversely, the full Logistics and Barman PDDL and description examples in v2 Appendix A are replaced by a repository link. Existing hardware, model defaults, and general code/data access information remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Valmeekam et al.'s study of o1 on PlanBench and explicitly questions prior claims of clear formalizer superiority. The central positioning around complete PDDL generation and natural descriptions remains, as does the related-work comparison table, renumbered from Table 7 to Table 1.

P1.justification: v3 extensively revises the findings and conclusion, expands explanations in Sections 2–4, and edits language throughout. The appendices are reorganized into explanatory sections with separately numbered listings, a new experimental-setup section, and a consolidated error-analysis section.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the performance plots, adds two graphical summaries of existing errors, and moves the detailed error tables into the appendix. BlocksWorld and Logistics tables now place naturalness settings side by side, prompting-result tables are added, and retained code examples become full-width numbered listings. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added DeepSeek-R1 comparisons and prompting analyses make v3 more informative and support better-qualified headline conclusions than v2's GPT-only formulation. The net gain is limited: new DeepSeek-R1 planner bars in Figure 3 disagree with Tables 3–4, Section 5.6 overgeneralizes the preference for planning on complex domains, and moving Logistics/Barman examples outside the PDF reduces self-contained documentation.
